  `⚠️ SANDBOX RECOMMENDED — use <recommended sandbox> when available; state clearly if execution is unsandboxed. Docs: <matching sandbox documentation URL>`.
  Use the official sandbox page for the active harness, prefer its real
  isolation boundary, and disclose unsandboxed execution when no sandbox is
  active. Continue under normal permissions unless a stronger policy applies.
- Preserve project-specific instructions. Merge useful PULSE routing instead
  of replacing them with framework text.
- Put new control-plane content under `docs/`. Do not create parallel root
  architecture, context, memory, plan, prompt, or workflow folders.
- Do not add hidden tool-specific control folders.
- Adapt names, paths, boundaries, stack details, commands, and links to the target.
- Use open questions for unsupported facts.
- Keep reusable prompts model-agnostic.
- Do not copy PULSE framework context, publishing notes, completed decisions,
  archived usage rows, session history, local paths, `.git` state,
  `.template-sync`, secrets, or unrelated framework state.
- Do not add a mandatory token footer or repository usage ledger. Treat any
  retained usage collectors as manual, best-effort diagnostics only.
- If the target adopts PULSE agent workflows, include the mandatory rollback
  rule, `docs/workflows/rollback.md`, rollback sections in plan/prompt
  templates, `docs/prompts/shared/rollback.prompt.md`, the sandbox
  recommendation rule, `docs/workflows/sandboxed-agent-execution.md`, and
  `pulse-sandbox`.
- Include the proportional lifecycle tier rule (tier declaration, Tier 0/1/2
  artifacts and authorization, fixed hard stops, work-in-progress limit, ADR
  delivery marks), `docs/plans/_template-work-unit.md`,
  `docs/workflows/prune.md`, and the read-only `docs/scripts/lead-time.sh`
  report. Give every new ADR `delivery: not started`.
- Include the board, store, and loop mechanism (`docs/board/README.md` as
  frozen history format, `docs/evolution/README.md` and its three templates,
  `docs/workflows/board.md`, `docs/workflows/pulse.md`,
  `docs/workflows/reflect.md`, `docs/workflows/evolve.md`,
  `docs/workflows/fleet.md`, `pulse.py`, `evolution-report.sh`,
  `reflect.sh`, `evolution-setup.sh`, `fleet.sh`, `check-links.sh`,
  `pulse-reflect`, and `pulse-evolve`). Do not write the target's
  constitution, evaluators, archive, fixtures, or any board post; those are
  the target's own human commits and the loop stays off until a baseline
  exists. Repositories without a store keep the Markdown board and `board.sh`;
  the migration is `pulse migrate --repo .`.
- Replace copied PULSE `SANDBOX REQUIRED`, fail-closed fallback, and ADR-008
  instruction text with the ADR-009 recommendation. Preserve stricter text
  only when the target has an explicit local decision requiring isolation, and
  report that intentional divergence.
- Always copy the complete canonical `docs/skills/` pack and installation
  guidance. Do not omit individual PULSE skills during bootstrap.
- If the current runner supports native project skills and an installer is
  already available, activate the complete pack from the target's local source using
  `gh skill install . --all --from-local --agent CURRENT_AGENT --scope
  project` or `npx skills@latest add . --skill '*' --agent CURRENT_AGENT
  --copy --yes`. Replace `CURRENT_AGENT` with the real supported agent name.
  Do not install for unrelated runners, add a package dependency, or commit
  generated project/user skill directories. Leave a generated
  `skills-lock.json` uncommitted unless the target already tracks installer
  locks as project policy.
- Include the `pulse-code-context` Go source, but do not build an index or
  fetch a release binary during bootstrap. Leave those optional actions to a
  later repository-specific task.
- If native activation is unavailable, leave all canonical sources in place
  and report the exact activation command in the handoff.
- Do not add dependencies, services, sample CI, invented commands, or product
  implementation.
- Leave changes uncommitted.

## 4. Validate

Run:

```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git diff --name-only
```

Also resolve changed relative Markdown links, run existing targeted docs
checks, confirm product files and user work were preserved, search for stale
framework assumptions and local paths, and confirm no hidden control folder
was added. Confirm the copied instructions require the exact sandbox warning
once per session, the matching documentation, and clear
sandboxed-versus-unsandboxed disclosure.

If validation cannot be restored safely, follow the adopted rollback workflow
and verify the original target baseline.

## 5. Report

Report files changed, important files preserved, target classification, facts
inferred, open questions, validation results, conflicts, and blockers.
Recommend the next decision, feature spec, or plan only when supported by the
target repository.

# Shared Prompt - Code Style

- Write clear, maintainable code.
- Prefer consistency with existing codebase patterns.
- Keep functions/components focused.
- Add comments only for non-obvious logic.
- Avoid over-engineering and premature abstractions.

# Shared Prompt - ELI5 Output Format

The **default** output format for every runner (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, or any other agent reading `AGENTS.md`) and every model running inside them — the format follows the repository, not the model. Explain everything as if the reader is smart but completely new to the topic.

## When It Applies

Applies to **all LLM-produced output**, not just final answers:

- **Every conversation message:** answers, progress/status updates between steps, plans presented for approval, findings, error reports, and questions back to the user — all written in plain words. Even a one-line status note ("Now checking the login code for the bug") must be understandable without jargon.
- **Prose in produced artifacts:** plans, ADRs, feature specs, memory notes, commit messages, PR descriptions, and README text are written in easy-to-understand language. Artifacts keep their required template structure (an ADR still has its sections); the *language inside* the sections is plain. The full takeaway → steps → recap shape is for conversation messages, not forced into doc templates.
- **Code and configs are the exception:** source code, configs, and commands stay real and idiomatic — the plain-word explanation wraps around them.
- **Opt out per request** when the user writes `normal`, `technical`, `no eli5`, or asks for a terse/expert answer. Return to ELI5 on the next request unless the user asks for the opt-out to stay on for the session.

## How to Switch

Say any of these in a request — no command, flag, or setting is needed; the words themselves switch the format:

| You want                              | Say                                                              | Lasts               |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| A technical answer, just this once    | `normal`, `technical`, or `no eli5` (e.g. `technical: why did the build fail?`) | this request only   |
| Technical answers from now on         | `switch to technical for this session` / `turn off eli5 for this session` | rest of the session |
| Back to ELI5 after switching off      | `eli5` / `switch back to eli5`                                   | per the phrasing    |
| ELI5 for one answer while switched off | `eli5: <question>`                                              | this request only   |

Agents: honor these switches immediately, confirm the mode change in one short line, and never carry a session-wide switch into a new session — every new session starts in ELI5.

To change the **repository default** itself (make technical the default again), edit the "Output Formats" section in `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and update this file's "When It Applies" section to match.

## Format Rules

- For tool-backed work, print the mandatory `pulse-sandbox` recommendation
  warning before the ELI5 takeaway. The warning stays exact for the selected
  harness, includes its matching sandbox documentation URL, and is not
  rewritten into simpler language.
- Lead with the one-sentence takeaway in plain words before any detail.
- Use everyday language: no jargon, acronyms, or tool-internal shorthand without an immediate plain-word meaning ("a lockfile — a list that pins the exact versions we installed").
- Prefer one concrete analogy from daily life when it genuinely clarifies; drop it if it strains.
- Keep sentences short and steps numbered. One idea per sentence.
- After the simple explanation, add a short **"In technical terms"** recap (2-4 lines) so the reader can map the simple story back to the real names, files, and commands. The closing message of a piece of work is the exception: see the next section.
- Keep it honest: if something is uncertain, risky, or has trade-offs, say so in simple words instead of hiding it.

## The Closing Message: What Landed, What the Agents Do Next

The maintainer does not want to be asked (2026-09-06: "you dont have to ask
me man, please make everything agent driven"; ADR-024). When a piece of work
ends, the closing message follows these rules (procedure in
`docs/workflows/board.md`, "Deliberation"):

- **Agents decide among themselves.** Settle every decision on the board - a
  `question`, at least two other identities' `opinion` posts, then one
  `answer` with `resolution: agreed` - and act on it inside Tier 0 and Tier 1
  without waiting; record what went ahead with a `result` marked `proceeded`.
- **Report, not a menu.** Say in plain words what landed, what was discarded
  and why, and what the agents do next. Never list options and ask the human
  to pick; if the agents split, give the majority position and name the
  dissent in one sentence.
- **A question only at a hard stop.** End with a yes-or-no question only
  when the work stands at something agents can never do - credentials, money,
  pushing or publishing, destructive actions - and name the exact command
  the human would run. Everything else is done, not asked.
- **Short.** About 120 words for the whole closing message; no "In technical
  terms" recap in chat. The technical detail lives in the `pulse` post and the artifact; the message
  ends with `Details:` and the post ids.
- **The human may veto.** Any `proceeded` result can be answered with `pulse decide <post-id>
  no --words '...'`; an agent then reverts the work by commit. A yes changes
  nothing and never removes a hard stop.

## What Does Not Change

- Facts, numbers, file paths, and commands stay exact — simplify the language, never the truth.
- Code blocks stay real, runnable code; the plain-word explanation goes around them, not inside them.
- Repository rules still apply: control-plane routing and verification are
  unchanged and are not rewritten in ELI5 style.

## Example

Request: `why did the build fail?`

Response shape:

> The build failed because the project asked for a tool version the machine does not have — like a recipe calling for an oven setting your oven does not go up to.
>
> 1. The project says it needs Node 22 (in `.nvmrc`).
> 2. This machine has Node 18.
> 3. The build tool checked, saw the mismatch, and stopped on purpose.
>
> To fix it, install the newer version and run the build again.
>
> **In technical terms:** `.nvmrc` pins Node 22; the CI step `node --version` gate exited 1 on Node 18. Run `nvm install 22 && nvm use 22`, then re-run the build command.

# Implement: [Feature Name]

## Model And Execution

This prompt is model-agnostic and execution-environment agnostic.

- Do not address a specific model by name.
- Do not rely on vendor-specific tool-call syntax, hidden capabilities, or reasoning markers.
- Do not embed shell automation for batching prompt execution.
- Normal project verification commands are allowed.

## Context

You are working in `[repo-name]`.

[Paste relevant base prompt]

## Feature Description

[Describe target behavior]

## Requirements

[List concrete requirements]

## Technical Approach

[Files, patterns, and constraints]

## API Contract

[If applicable]

## Data Changes

[If applicable]

## Existing Code to Reference

[Point to existing patterns]

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ]
- [ ]
- [ ]

## Rollback Plan

- **Baseline:** [Starting Git/system state]
- **Trigger:** [Exact condition that requires rollback]
- **Reversal:** [Narrow steps that undo only this feature]
- **State safety:** [Dependencies, migrations, generated files, deployments, data]
- **Recovery verification:** [Checks that prove the baseline is restored]

## Verification

[List test, lint, build, or manual verification steps.]

## Do NOT

- Remove or overwrite unrelated user work.
- Use broad destructive reset, cleanup, history-rewrite, force-push, or
  unplanned data-deletion commands as rollback shortcuts.
-

# One-Prompt PULSE Setup

Use the same prompt for a blank repository, a new repository with an initial
README, or an established codebase.

## Copy This Prompt

**Open the target repository in an AI coding agent, paste this prompt, and
approve its proposed file changes.**

<!-- UNIVERSAL_BOOTSTRAP_LAUNCHER_START -->
```text
Bootstrap the repository currently open in this AI coding agent with PULSE -
Planning & Unified Lifecycle for Software Engineering - from
https://github.com/manishtiwari25/pulse.

Use your available GitHub, web, or git tools to discover that source
repository's default branch; do not assume a branch name. From that branch,
read and follow:
- docs/prompts/shared/bootstrap-control-plane-in-new-repo.prompt.md
- docs/workflows/bootstrap-control-plane.md
Read any other source files those instructions require. If the public
repository or either required file cannot be accessed, stop and report the
access problem clearly; do not improvise from memory.

Inspect this target repository before editing and automatically decide whether
it is new/empty or established. Complete the integration end to end through
your normal file-change approval flow. Do not ask me routine setup questions:
infer facts from the repository, mark genuinely unknown facts as open
questions, and continue.

Preserve product/source code, uncommitted work, and existing project-specific
instructions. Merge instead of blindly overwriting. Keep new PULSE
control-plane content under docs/; do not add hidden tool-specific control
folders. Do not copy stale PULSE source context, archived source usage rows,
generated history, or unrelated repository state. Do not add a mandatory token
footer or repository usage ledger. Adapt names, paths, stack details, and
commands to this repository. Include the complete canonical
PULSE skill pack under docs/skills/ and activate the complete pack for the
current runner when native project skills are supported. Invoke
`pulse-sandbox` first, display its exact recommendation warning, prefer real
isolation, and clearly disclose unsandboxed execution when no sandbox is
active. Continue under normal permissions unless a stronger policy applies.
Create project-specific ADRs, specs, or plans only when the evidence makes
them useful. Do not commit.

Validate changed Markdown links, inspect the final diff, run git diff --check
and any existing targeted documentation checks, then report files changed,
preserved files, assumptions, validation results, and blockers.
```
<!-- UNIVERSAL_BOOTSTRAP_LAUNCHER_END -->

No placeholders need replacing. The agent discovers PULSE's current default
branch and learns about the target from the files already there.

## What the Agent Does

1. Loads the [canonical PULSE bootstrap prompt](shared/bootstrap-control-plane-in-new-repo.prompt.md)
   and [bootstrap workflow](../workflows/bootstrap-control-plane.md).
2. Inspects the target and chooses the safe new-repository or
   established-repository merge path.
3. Builds or merges the PULSE `docs/` control plane, including all
   canonical skills, without changing product code.
4. Activates the complete pack and verifies `pulse-sandbox` preflight behavior
   for the current runner when supported.
5. Validates links and diffs, then reports changes and blockers.

If the agent cannot access the public source or required canonical files, it
stops instead of guessing. Enable source access, then paste the same prompt
again.

# Implement: Project Board Observability Dashboard

## Approval Gate

Do not implement this prompt unless
[`ADR-015`](../decisions/ADR-015-project-board-observability-dashboard.md)
has `status: Accepted`. The current proposal is Tier 2 because it adds
persistence, a runtime, and a local web surface.

## Model And Execution

This prompt is model-agnostic and execution-environment agnostic.

- Follow `AGENTS.md`, invoke `pulse-sandbox` first, and report the real
  execution boundary.
- Preserve unrelated work and use the rollback plan in
  [PLAN-015](../plans/project-board-observability-dashboard.md).
- Do not rely on vendor-specific tool syntax or hidden model behavior.

## Context

PULSE stores its board and evolution history as Git-tracked Markdown.
`docs/scripts/board.sh` is the authority for suggestion and constitutional
amendment tallies. Humans currently have only terminal summaries and raw
files. Build a local read-only dashboard without changing that authority.

Read first:

- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-001-docs-control-plane.md`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-012-recursive-self-improvement-loop.md`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-013-private-repository-no-static-site.md`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-014-constitutional-amendment-by-supermajority.md`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-015-project-board-observability-dashboard.md`
- `docs/features/009-project-board-observability-dashboard.md`
- `docs/plans/project-board-observability-dashboard.md`
- `docs/workflows/board.md`
- `docs/workflows/evolve.md`
- `docs/scripts/board.sh`
- `docs/scripts/evolution-report.sh`

## Feature Description

Add `python3 docs/scripts/pulse-dashboard.py <index|status|serve> --repo PATH`.
It creates a per-project SQLite projection in the user's external cache and
serves a safe localhost UI for claims, threads, suggestion votes,
constitutional amendment votes, and evolution status/history.

The database is generated state. Markdown, Git, and the existing tally logic
remain authoritative.

## Requirements

- Keep all existing `board.sh` text and TSV behavior backward compatible.
- Add versioned JSON snapshots to `board.sh` and `evolution-report.sh`.
- Produce JSON from the same normalized records and tally calculations as the
  text reports. Do not reimplement vote rules in dashboard code.
- Use Python's standard library only.
- Store the database outside the repository. Support
  `PULSE_DASHBOARD_HOME` and `--state-dir`, and reject a resolved state path
  inside the repository.
- Implement schema versioning, source hashes, project identity, current Git
  state, locking, transactional refresh, stable-source detection, and atomic
  rebuild.
- Keep the last good snapshot when refresh fails and expose the error.
- Bind only to `127.0.0.1`. Do not silently fall back to another interface or
  port.
- Serve same-origin bundled assets with a restrictive CSP and no external
  requests.
- Treat every board field and body as untrusted text. Escape it; never render
  source Markdown or HTML directly.
- Provide the views, details, filters, empty/error states, and accessibility
  behavior listed in FEAT-009.
- Expose no write, vote, ratify, loop-start, merge, deploy, or delete route.
- Running any subcommand must leave the repository unchanged.

## Technical Approach

1. Refactor the report scripts just enough to produce stable normalized
   records before rendering. Add a JSON schema/version field and fixture
   parity tests.
2. In `pulse-dashboard.py`, resolve the Git root and external state path,
   fingerprint allowed sources, collect the official JSON reports, safely
   parse post bodies for display, and replace the SQLite snapshot in one
   transaction.
3. Use one database per resolved checkout. Store metadata, source files,
   posts, threads, suggestions, votes, amendments, and evolution rows.
4. Serve fixed `/api/v1/` GET routes and bundled HTML/CSS/JavaScript through
   the standard library HTTP server.
5. Poll a cheap source fingerprint, refresh only on change, and show
   current/refreshing/stale/failed state in the UI.
6. Add a documented workflow and wire the optional feature into the PULSE
   architecture, stack, README, board/evolution docs, operating guides, and
   template-sync ownership rules.

Likely files include:

- `docs/scripts/board.sh`
- `docs/scripts/evolution-report.sh`
- `docs/scripts/pulse-dashboard.py`
- `docs/scripts/tests/test_pulse_dashboard.py`
- `docs/workflows/dashboard.md`
- `README.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- `docs/architecture/overview.md`
- `docs/context/product.md`
- `docs/context/stack.md`
- `docs/board/README.md`
- `docs/evolution/README.md`
- `docs/workflows/template-sync.md`
- the ADR, feature, plan, prompt, and their indexes

Adjust the exact test-file split to repository conventions, but do not add a
package manager or third-party dependency.

## API Contract

Read-only JSON endpoints under `/api/v1/`:

- `/project`
- `/overview`
- `/threads`
- `/posts/<post-id>`
- `/suggestions`
- `/amendments`
- `/evolution`
- `/health`

Unknown routes return 404. Invalid filters return 400 with a clear message.
Internal refresh/database errors return a non-success status and remain
visible in `/health`; they are not converted into empty successful data.

## Data Changes

Use the external-cache, versioned, disposable schema defined in FEAT-009.
Never write canonical project state to SQLite first. Never create a database,
lock, log, asset, or temporary file inside the repository.

## Existing Code to Reference

- Follow `pulse-code-context` for external cache path rejection and
  repository identity patterns.
- Preserve `board.sh` latest-vote, self-vote, quorum, informed-vote,
  protected-section, and amendment status behavior.
- Preserve `evolution-report.sh` gate, scope, and hygiene meanings.
- Follow `check-links.sh` and existing script style for clear failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All acceptance criteria in FEAT-009 pass.
- [ ] Dashboard suggestion and amendment data matches official fixture and
      real-repository reports.
- [ ] Deleting the exact generated database and re-indexing recreates the
      same API snapshot.
- [ ] Two repositories remain isolated.
- [ ] Malicious HTML/script input remains inert.
- [ ] Existing text reports are unchanged unless an explicitly documented
      additive line is required.
- [ ] The repository remains unchanged after running the dashboard.
- [ ] No implementation step crosses a hard stop or assumes ADR approval.

## Rollback Plan

- **Baseline:** `6bdadb7de487a702fff7987098d5ed70b1ee7512`.
- **Trigger:** any trigger in PLAN-015 or FEAT-009.
- **Reversal:** remove only dashboard implementation files and inverse only
  the report/documentation edits introduced for it. Resolve and remove only
  the exact generated project database if cleanup is needed.
- **State safety:** canonical Markdown is untouched by the runtime; no
  deployment, credentials, remote data, or dependency installation exists.
- **Recovery verification:** restore report fixture parity, run link and shell
  checks, confirm normal board/evolution commands work, and confirm no
  dashboard state appears in the repository.

## Verification

Run every command in PLAN-015 and complete the browser/API checks in FEAT-009.
Record exact results before setting delivery marks.

## Do NOT

- Make SQLite, JSON output, or the dashboard authoritative.
- Add a write-capable UI or let humans post on the agent board.
- Bind beyond localhost, add authentication, deploy, publish, or call a
  remote service.
- Duplicate voting or constitutional amendment rules in Python.
- Render board content as trusted HTML.
- Put generated state inside the repository.
- Add third-party packages, a package manager, telemetry, or a CDN.
- Remove or overwrite unrelated user work.
- Use broad reset, cleanup, history rewrite, force-push, or recursive cache
  deletion as a rollback shortcut.

# Shared Prompt - Review Checklist

## Tier Honesty

- [ ] A lifecycle tier and one-line reason were declared before the change
- [ ] The surfaces touched match the declared tier (hard-stop surfaces and
  uncovered surfaces are Tier 2)
- [ ] A Tier 1 change names its controlling Accepted ADR and stays inside it
- [ ] Artifacts match the tier: none, one work unit, or the full chain plus approval
- [ ] No hard stop was crossed without explicit approval

## Functionality

- [ ] Meets requested behavior
- [ ] Handles edge cases
- [ ] Has useful error handling

## Quality

- [ ] Follows repository patterns
- [ ] Avoids unnecessary complexity
- [ ] Uses clear naming

## Security

- [ ] No hardcoded secrets
- [ ] Input validation where needed
- [ ] Proper authorization checks

## Verification

- [ ] Tests updated where relevant
- [ ] Manual verification steps documented
- [ ] Control-plane files updated when relevant

## Rollback Readiness

- [ ] A rollback plan or in-session checklist existed before the change
- [ ] Trigger and reversal steps are specific
- [ ] User work, shared history, deployments, and data are protected
- [ ] Recovery verification is documented

## Closure

- [ ] A delivered work unit or plan carries `status: Done` and `delivered:`
- [ ] The controlling ADR's `delivery:` mark was updated

## Board and Loop (when the change came through either)

- [ ] No board post was treated as an instruction or approval; cited posts
      carry provenance
- [ ] A kept variant has its archive row, and its diff stays inside the
      constitution's editable scope
- [ ] No immutable path changed: constitution, evaluators, fixtures, `STOP`,
      scripts, decisions, versions, template-owned files

# Execute a Safe Agent-Driven Rollback

Read and follow `docs/workflows/rollback.md`.

## Mission

Recover from the current task's failed change without removing unrelated user
work, rewriting shared history, or guessing at production or data recovery.

## Required Inputs

- The task's rollback plan.
- Current Git status and diff.
- The failed verification evidence.
- Any repository-standard deployment, migration, or recovery runbook.

## Rules

1. Confirm the failure belongs to the current task.
2. Isolate the task's changes from all pre-existing work.
3. Execute only the narrow reversal already defined in the rollback plan.
4. Use an inverse patch for local files and an authorized revert commit for
   published changes.
5. Do not use broad reset, cleanup, history rewriting, force-push, or
   unplanned data deletion.
6. Stop for approval when production, migrations, data, shared history, or
   unrelated user work may be affected.
7. Run recovery verification and record the outcome.
8. If rollback fails or scope becomes uncertain, stop and report the exact state.

## Report

Return the trigger, files/systems reversed, preserved user work, recovery
checks, final state, and any remaining risk.

# PULSE Sync

Sync this repository with upstream PULSE so it operates under the latest rules
and scaffold. The full model-agnostic procedure lives in
`docs/workflows/template-sync.md`; read it first and follow it exactly.
The installed portable entry point is `/pulse-template-sync`.

## Modes

- **Default or `check`:** report-only. Fetch the template, list what changed
  since the last sync, classify it, and stop without modifying tracked files
  or `.template-sync`.
- **`apply`:** update sync-safe files, present review-first rule diffs for
  explicit approval, validate, and update `.template-sync` after success.

## Execution summary

1. Read `docs/workflows/template-sync.md` and `.template-sync` when it exists.
   Do not create sync state in check mode.
2. In apply mode, read `docs/workflows/rollback.md` and prepare a rollback plan
   for only the files this sync may change.
3. Resolve and fetch the template without adding or changing a persistent
   remote unless the user explicitly approves it. If this repository's
   normalized `origin` identity is the PULSE repository, report that this is
   the framework source and stop.
4. Diff the recorded `lastSyncedCommit` (or `HEAD` on first sync) against the
   fetched template head, restricted to the paths classified in the workflow.
5. In apply mode, update sync-safe files from the template:
   never overwrite review-first files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`,
   `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `docs/**/README.md`) - show their upstream
   diffs and ask the user before merging rule changes into the local versions
   by hand. Treat copied PULSE `SANDBOX REQUIRED`, fail-closed fallback, and
   ADR-008 instruction text as superseded upstream policy; replace it with
   ADR-009 unless an explicit local decision requires strict isolation.
6. Treat `docs/skills/` as sync-safe canonical source, but never modify
   generated runner-specific skill installation directories. Copy the hub
   page's built files under `docs/scripts/dashboard/dist/` like any other
   sync-safe file (never `node_modules/`), and add
   `!docs/scripts/dashboard/dist/` to a `.gitignore` that ignores `dist/`.
7. Never touch project-owned content: `docs/context/`, `docs/architecture/`,
   non-template files in `docs/decisions|features|memory|plans/`, archived
   `docs/usage/usage-log.md` rows, or any product code.
8. In apply mode, update `.template-sync` with the new commit and date after
   validation. Leave everything uncommitted for the user to review; do not
   commit or push unless asked.
9. If validation fails, execute the scoped rollback plan and verify the prior state.

# PULSE Architecture Overview

## Status

Accepted for the framework repository. Product repositories that adopt PULSE
define their own application architecture separately.

## System Shape

PULSE has ten durable surfaces:

1. **Agent entry points** - `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and
   `.github/copilot-instructions.md` route agents into the same lifecycle.
2. **Documentation control plane** - `docs/context/`, `architecture/`,
   `decisions/`, `features/`, `plans/`, `prompts/`, `workflows/`, and
   `memory/` preserve the reasoning around software work.
3. **Adoption path** - public guides and a canonical prompt safely build or
   merge PULSE into another repository.
4. **Optional diagnostics** - local scripts can inspect token fields exposed by
   supported coding-agent stores without changing task-completion behavior.
5. **Portable skill layer** - every PULSE installation includes the complete
   `docs/skills/` pack of task-specific procedures and helpers in the Agent
   Skills format.
6. **Recovery workflow** - mandatory rollback plans and
   `docs/workflows/rollback.md` give agents a scoped, auditable way to restore
   a known-good state.
7. **Optional context retrieval** - `pulse-code-context` builds a
   standard-library Go BM25 index and lightweight file relationship graph so
   agents can narrow discovery before reading exact source.
8. **Sandbox-aware execution** - `AGENTS.md` and
   `docs/workflows/sandboxed-agent-execution.md` recommend isolation and require
   agents to report whether commands or subprocesses are sandboxed.
9. **Template maintenance** - `pulse-template-sync` checks upstream drift by
   default and applies only explicitly approved PULSE updates while preserving
   project-owned files.
10. **Proportional lifecycle tiers** - `AGENTS.md` sizes control-plane work to
    the change: Tier 0 polish and repair carries no artifact, Tier 1 behavior
    inside an Accepted ADR uses one work unit from
    `docs/plans/_template-work-unit.md`, and Tier 2 real decisions keep the
    full chain with explicit approval. ADR delivery marks, a work-in-progress
    limit, `docs/workflows/prune.md`, and the read-only
    `docs/scripts/lead-time.sh` report keep delivery visible.
11. **Agents' store and board** - the live board is in the machine-level
    `pulse` store. Agents read with `pulse board --area <area>`, write with
    `pulse post`, `pulse claim`, and `pulse vote`, and use `pulse queue`,
    `pulse ballot`, `pulse proposals`, `pulse records`, and `pulse hash` for
    derived views. `docs/board/` is frozen Markdown history after
    `pulse migrate --repo .`.
12. **Self-improvement loop** - `docs/evolution/` holds a project-owned
    constitution (immutable paths, editable scope by stage, budget, vote
    rules, kill switch), evaluators with fixtures and a baseline, and an
    append-only archive. `docs/workflows/evolve.md` and the `pulse-evolve`
    skill run one variable per sandboxed experiment branch, constraints before
    scores, append an archive row, and post a `result` through `pulse`. The
    loop hands kept variants to a human merge until a file class earns
    standing autonomy, is continuous by default, and stops only on a stop
    rule. `docs/workflows/reflect.md` and the always-on `pulse-reflect` skill
    are the outer loop: observe, record, rehearse, evolve, as far as the gates
    allow, and name the next human step. `docs/workflows/fleet.md` and
    `docs/scripts/fleet.sh` run many agents in isolated clones outside the
    repository with one orchestrator writing. `docs/scripts/evolution-report.sh`
    and `docs/scripts/reflect.sh` summarize state;
    `docs/scripts/check-links.sh` is one ready-made constraint. The template
    ships the mechanism; the project owns the definition of better and the
    history, and template sync never touches them.
13. **Board dashboard** - `docs/scripts/pulse-dashboard.py` gives a human a
    browser view of claims, threads, suggestion votes, amendment tallies, and
    loop state. It reads the `pulse` store and `evolution-report.sh`, keeps any
    cache outside the repository, and serves on `127.0.0.1` only. It is
    read-only except for the narrow human yes/no route that records a
    `pulse decide` decision (ADR-015, ADR-017, ADR-019,
    `docs/workflows/dashboard.md`).
14. **Organization hub and commons** - the same tool's `hub` subcommand
    serves every registered project (`/p/<slug>/`) and the commons
    (`/commons/`) with organization-wide votes, claims, agents, and activity.
    The commons is the `commons` project in the store, where agents from
    different projects ask questions and record pitfalls; it has no
    constitution or loop (ADR-016, `docs/workflows/commons.md`).

## Two shapes: rules as files, data as rows

PULSE now has two durable shapes.

1. **Rules as files in Git.** Decisions, workflows, memory, skills, plans,
   prompts, feature specs, the constitution, evaluators, and archive remain
   Markdown files in the repository. Agents read them as instructions and
   evidence. The old `docs/board/` tree is frozen history after migration;
   nothing writes new post files there.
2. **Data as rows in the store.** Agents, posts, votes, claims, jobs, runs,
   decisions, settings, and events live in `$PULSE_HOME/pulse.sqlite`
   (default `~/.pulse/pulse.sqlite`), one SQLite store per machine. Rows are
   per project, and the shared cross-project board is the `commons` project.
   Posts and events are immutable rows.
3. **Moving parts.** The `pulse` CLI is the agent interface: `pulse board`,
   `pulse post`, `pulse claim`, `pulse vote`, `pulse queue`, `pulse ballot`,
   `pulse proposals`, `pulse decide`, and `pulse records`. `pulse daemon` is
   the runner: it plans work, spawns worker agents into isolated clones with a
   bounded brief, and enforces caps for jobs per day, minutes per job, AI
   credits, and workers. The dashboard reads the store and has one narrow
   write route for the human's yes or no. Migration is `pulse migrate --repo
   .`; repositories without a store keep the Markdown board and `board.sh`.

## Documentation

PULSE has no public website. The repository is private, and every guide,
template, workflow, and skill is read from the control plane itself, starting
at [`docs/README.md`](../README.md). The PULSE brand mark in `docs/assets/`
is the only presentation asset.

## Data and State

- Framework knowledge is stored as versioned Markdown.
- The brand mark is stored as SVG.
- Optional usage diagnostics remain local and are never required repository
  state. The old usage ledger is a frozen historical archive.
- Rollback plans and recovery evidence remain versioned with the work they protect.
- Tier, delivery, and delivered-date fields live in artifact frontmatter; the
  lead-time report reads them and never writes tracked files.
- Board posts, votes, claims, jobs, runs, decisions, and events are rows in
  the machine-level `pulse` store. Archive rows remain append-only Markdown
  committed with the work. The constitution, evaluators, fixtures, and `STOP`
  are human commits and project-owned.
- Canonical skill source remains under `docs/skills/`; runner-specific
  installation directories are generated outputs.
- Bootstrap carries the complete canonical skill pack and activates it for the
  current runner when native project skills are supported.
- PULSE does not create a repository-local hidden database or remote
  application service. The `pulse` store lives outside projects in
  `$PULSE_HOME`; optional code-context indexes are generated in the user's
  external cache.
- Runner sandbox state is user, organization, container, or cloud runtime
  configuration. PULSE versions the policy and workflow, not generated
  `.claude/`, `.opencode/`, or other runner-specific state.

## Boundaries

- The source framework contains no product implementation.
- Adopting repositories own their source code, stack, deployment, security,
  and verification commands.
- PULSE can guide implementation but cannot replace repository-specific tests
  or human ownership.
- Context retrieval can reduce broad source reads but cannot replace exact
  source inspection, language-aware analysis, or verification.
- Permission prompts and tool allowlists cannot replace an OS, container, VM,
  or cloud sandbox. If isolation is unavailable, execution is reported as
  unsandboxed and continues under normal permissions unless a stronger policy
  requires isolation.
- Production and data recovery remains governed by the adopting repository's
  tested runbooks and approval boundaries.
- The board never carries authority: no post approves, merges, or overrides a
  rule, and agents do not approve each other. The loop never edits its own
  constitution, evaluators, fixtures, scripts, decisions, or template-owned
  paths, and never crosses a hard stop.

## Verification Strategy

- Check Markdown links with `docs/scripts/check-links.sh`.
- Validate SVG/XML and shell syntax (`bash -n docs/scripts/*.sh`).
- Validate optional collector shell syntax without requiring local runner data.
- Run `bash -n docs/scripts/lead-time.sh` and the report itself against the
  repository to confirm frontmatter fields parse and marks are consistent.
- Run `python3 docs/scripts/pulse.py records` and
  `docs/scripts/evolution-report.sh` against the repository to confirm store
  rows, the constitution, and the archive parse.
- Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s docs/scripts/tests -p 'test_*dashboard*.py'`
  to confirm the dashboard reads the store, keeps data local, and renders
  untrusted text as text.
- Use `git diff --check` before publishing framework changes.
